findings.summary: Phase 5 lifecycle-fence MEDIUM is closed; a Prepared record may still be written after a drain enumeration, but no mutation/commit can cross the fence and the record is immediately aborted (terminal).
findings.detail: Verified by code inspection and by the interleaved test FenceRaisedAfterPreparationAbortsBeforeAnyMutation: ArtworkPublisher now re-reads the durable fence immediately before the first mutation (aborts without an external effect) and again immediately before the final PublishedArtworkState commit (leaves the verified FinalizationPending postcondition for reconciliation). The invariant is: a mutation/commit implies the operation was durable before the drain's Enumerate (Prepared before the pre-mutation check; FinalizationPending before the pre-commit check), and the drain's per-subject reconcile serializes with the publisher through ArtworkSubjectGate, so a committed Published state is seen by the drain and restored. In the test's paused-capture interleaving the publication does write Prepared after the drain enumerated, but it then aborts before any mutation; the durable outcome is terminal, so no untracked non-terminal publication survives. This satisfies the finding's recommended action/recommended barrier and the reviewer requirement that no untracked non-terminal publication survives the fence.

findings.summary: Generation fence is enforced by the store; creation of superseding artwork work is intentionally deferred to 6.6.
findings.detail: ArtworkOperationStore.Write -> EnsureWriteIsFenced throws InvalidOperationException on a stale generation, and ArtworkRecoveryGate's postcondition fails closed (Blocked) when the re-read durable generation is older than the reconciled record (ArtworkOperationFencing.IsStale). The gate exposes the authoritative durable generation, but 6.4 does not itself create a superseding publication operation from metadata; docs/implementation/6.4/worker-report.json discloses this and fingerprint-driven creation is task 6.6. This is consistent with the task scope and not a defect.
